dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: This local definition is the complete proposition: there exists a real constant c with 0 < c such that a uniform exponential upper-tail inequality holds for every finite family of independent, measurable, almost-everywhere bounded real-valued random variables on every probability space.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies all mathematical content hidden behind the elaborated target type, including the global existential witness, the order of all universal binders and hypotheses, and the exact no-prefactor exponential conclusion with the full range-square sum as denominator.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical conjunction of two propositions.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It conjoins positivity of the existential constant c with the universal tail-bound property required of that same c.

dependency_coverage.name: DivInvMonoid.toDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: It extracts the division operation from a division-and-inversion monoid structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Together with the real-number instance, it makes the quotient in the exponent ordinary total real division.

dependency_coverage.name: Exists
dependency_coverage.meaning: Existential quantification over a witness satisfying a predicate.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It places one witness c before all later universal binders, so c is independent of the index type, probability space, random variables, bounds, and threshold.

dependency_coverage.name: Filter.Eventually
dependency_coverage.meaning: A predicate holds eventually in a filter when its truth set belongs to that filter.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Applied to the almost-everywhere filter of μ, it states that X i lies in the closed interval [m i, M i] for μ-almost every outcome, separately for each i.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.sum
dependency_coverage.meaning: The finite sum of the values of a function over a finite set in an additive commutative monoid.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms both the finite centered random sum over all indices and the finite sum of squared interval widths in the exponent denominator.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.univ
dependency_coverage.meaning: The finite set containing every element of a type equipped with a Fintype instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes both displayed sums range over every index i in ι.

dependency_coverage.name: Fintype
dependency_coverage.meaning: A structure giving a finite enumeration of all elements of a type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It restricts the indexed family to an arbitrary finite index type and enables the two sums over all indices.

dependency_coverage.name: GE.ge
dependency_coverage.meaning: The relation a ≥ b, defined as b ≤ a.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines the upper-tail event by the inclusive condition that the centered sum is at least t.

dependency_coverage.name: HDiv.hDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: The heterogeneous division operation selected by an HDiv instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Here all operands are real, so it divides c t^2 by the entire finite sum of squared real norms; Lean real division remains defined even if that entire denominator is zero.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: The heterogeneous multiplication operation selected by an HMul instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Here it is real multiplication and forms exactly c times t squared in the numerator, with no additional coefficient or prefactor.

dependency_coverage.name: HPow.hPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: The power operation selected by an HPow instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Using the natural exponent 2, it squares t and separately squares each norm ||M i - m i||.

dependency_coverage.name: HSub.hSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: The heterogeneous subtraction operation selected by an HSub instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: As real subtraction, it centers each X i by subtracting its μ-integral and forms each interval difference M i - m i.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: The non-strict order relation supplied by an LE instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the non-strict conclusion μ.real(event) ≤ exponential bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.meaning: The strict order relation supplied by an LT instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For reals, it requires both the global constant c and the threshold t to be strictly positive.

dependency_coverage.name: Measurable
dependency_coverage.meaning: A function is measurable when the preimage of every measurable set is measurable.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It explicitly requires every coordinate random variable X i : Ω → ℝ to be measurable for the supplied measurable structure on Ω and the Borel structure on ℝ.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasurableSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: A measurable-space structure specifying the measurable subsets of a type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It equips the arbitrary outcome type Ω with the σ-algebra used by μ, measurability, almost-everywhere assertions, and integration.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure
dependency_coverage.meaning: A proposition-valued typeclass asserting that a measure is a probability measure, in particular normalized to total mass one.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It restricts μ to a probability measure, so the left side is a finite real probability and almost-everywhere bounds cannot evade a positive-mass whole space.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Measure
dependency_coverage.meaning: A countably additive nonnegative measure on a measurable space, taking set values in the extended nonnegative reals.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies μ, the common probability measure used for independence, almost-everywhere bounds, expectations, and the upper-tail event probability.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike
dependency_coverage.meaning: It coerces a measure to its set function, sending each set to an extended-nonnegative-real measure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the underlying evaluation used when the event set is measured and then converted to a real number.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.instOuterMeasureClass
dependency_coverage.meaning: It provides the outer-measure interface for measures.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It enables construction of μ's almost-everywhere filter used in the coordinatewise interval hypotheses.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.Measure.real
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a measure μ and set s, this is the real number obtained by applying ENNReal.toReal to μ(s).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the left side a real-valued event probability. The probability-measure assumption ensures the relevant measure is finite, so this agrees with the ordinary real probability rather than encountering an infinite value.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.ae
dependency_coverage.meaning: The almost-everywhere filter associated with a measure, whose eventual predicates fail only on a null set.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets each interval bound m i ≤ X i ≤ M i as holding μ-almost everywhere, not pointwise for every outcome.

dependency_coverage.name: MeasureTheory.integral
dependency_coverage.meaning: The Bochner integral of a function with respect to a measure, returned as an element of the normed real vector space; in Lean it is a total operation even outside explicit integrability hypotheses.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For each i it supplies ∫ X i dμ, the centering constant subtracted from X i(ω). No separate integrability assumption appears in the proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: Membership.mem
dependency_coverage.meaning: The membership relation supplied by a Membership instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With set membership, it asserts X i(ω) belongs to the closed interval Set.Icc (m i) (M i).

dependency_coverage.name: Monoid.toNatPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: It derives natural-number exponentiation from a monoid's repeated multiplication operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For real numbers it interprets exponent 2 as ordinary squaring in t^2 and ||M i - m i||^2.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of natural numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the exponent type for the literal exponent 2 in both sets of squares.

dependency_coverage.name: Neg.neg
dependency_coverage.meaning: Unary negation supplied by a Neg instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For reals it negates the complete quotient (c t^2)/(sum_i ||M i - m i||^2) before applying exp.

dependency_coverage.name: Norm.norm
dependency_coverage.meaning: The norm operation taking an element of a normed type to a real number.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For each real interval difference M i - m i it produces its real norm, which is then squared in the denominator.

dependency_coverage.name: NormedField.toNormedSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: A normed field is canonically a normed vector space over itself.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the real normed-space structure needed for the real-valued Bochner integrals of the X i.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: It interprets a natural-number literal in a target type through an OfNat instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets 0 as a real in positivity comparisons and 2 as the natural exponent used by the power operations.

dependency_coverage.name: ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun
dependency_coverage.meaning: It asserts mutual independence of an indexed family of measurable-target functions with respect to a measure, expressed via the corresponding constant kernel and a Dirac base measure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Applied to X and μ, it requires the entire finite family (X i) to be jointly independent under μ, not merely pairwise independent.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The constant c, the random-variable values, lower and upper bounds, threshold, integrals, norms, exponential, and final inequality are all real-valued.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.exp
dependency_coverage.meaning: The ordinary real exponential function.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It produces exactly exp(-(c t^2)/(sum_i ||M i - m i||^2)) as the right-hand side, with no multiplicative prefactor outside the exponential.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: The additive commutative monoid structure on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies real addition and zero for both finite sums, including the empty-index sum.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instDivInvMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: The division-and-inversion monoid structure on the real numbers, whose division is total in Lean.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the exponent quotient as real division and makes division by a zero denominator equal to the Lean real value obtained from inverse zero, namely zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: The usual non-strict order ≤ on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the final comparison as the ordinary real inequality between event probability and the exponential bound.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLT
dependency_coverage.meaning: The usual strict order < on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets 0 < c and 0 < t as strict real positivity.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: The multiplicative monoid structure on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports natural powers such as t^2 and ||M i - m i||^2.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: The ordinary multiplication operation on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the numerator exactly c multiplied by t^2.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instNeg
dependency_coverage.meaning: The ordinary additive negation operation on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It places a minus sign around the complete quotient in the exponential exponent.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instPreorder
dependency_coverage.meaning: The usual preorder structure on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the real order used to define the closed intervals [m i, M i].

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real subtraction, defined as addition of the additive inverse.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets X i(ω) - ∫X i dμ and M i - m i as ordinary real differences.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: The zero element of the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the real zero used in the strict positivity conditions for c and t and in total-division boundary behavior.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.measurableSpace
dependency_coverage.meaning: The Borel measurable-space structure on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines the codomain measurable structure for every measurable random variable X i.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.norm
dependency_coverage.meaning: The norm on ℝ, defined by ||r|| = |r|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes each denominator term ||M i - m i||^2 equal |M i - m i|^2, hence the square of the interval-width magnitude.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.normedAddCommGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: The normed additive commutative group structure on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It provides the normed additive codomain structure required for real Bochner integration.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.normedField
dependency_coverage.meaning: The normed field structure on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the compatible real scalar, field, norm, and division structures used by integration and by the arithmetic in the exponent.

dependency_coverage.name: Set
dependency_coverage.meaning: A set of α is represented as a predicate α → Prop.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It represents both the closed intervals in ℝ and the subset of Ω defining the upper-tail event.

dependency_coverage.name: Set.Icc
dependency_coverage.meaning: The closed order interval [a,b] = {x | a ≤ x and x ≤ b}.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For every index i it expresses the almost-everywhere two-sided bound m i ≤ X i(ω) ≤ M i.

dependency_coverage.name: Set.instMembership
dependency_coverage.meaning: The usual membership instance for predicate-represented sets.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It turns membership of X i(ω) in Set.Icc (m i) (M i) into the interval-bound proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: Zero.toOfNat0
dependency_coverage.meaning: It interprets the numeral 0 of a type as that type's zero element.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For reals it supplies the zero in 0 < c and 0 < t.

dependency_coverage.name: instHDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: It lifts a homogeneous division operation on α to an HDiv α α α instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It selects ordinary real division for the numerator divided by the complete denominator sum.

dependency_coverage.name: instHMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: It lifts a homogeneous multiplication operation on α to an HMul α α α instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It selects ordinary real multiplication for c times t squared.

dependency_coverage.name: instHPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: It lifts a power operation Pow α β to the corresponding heterogeneous HPow α β α instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It selects real-to-natural-number exponentiation for all exponent-2 expressions.

dependency_coverage.name: instHSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: It lifts a homogeneous subtraction operation on α to an HSub α α α instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It selects ordinary real subtraction in both the centered summands and interval differences.

dependency_coverage.name: instOfNatNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: It interprets each natural-number literal n as the natural number n itself.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the natural exponent value 2 passed to real exponentiation.

dependency_coverage.name: setOf
dependency_coverage.meaning: It forms a set from its membership predicate.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It constructs the event {ω | sum_i (X i(ω) - ∫X i dμ) ≥ t} whose μ-measure appears on the left side.

binders: There exists a real number c, chosen before all subsequent data.
The witness c is required to satisfy 0 < c.
Universally quantify over arbitrary types ι and Ω, with ι equipped with a finite-type structure and Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
Universally quantify over a measure μ on Ω, together with an instance asserting that μ is a probability measure.

Universally quantify over a family X : ι → Ω → ℝ of real-valued functions, lower- and upper-bound functions m,M : ι → ℝ, and a threshold t : ℝ. All of these binders occur after c, so c cannot depend on any of them.
hypotheses: For every i in ι, the function X_i : Ω → ℝ is measurable (with ℝ carrying its Borel σ-algebra).
The family (X_i) indexed by ι is mutually independent with respect to μ.
For every i in ι, X_i(ω) belongs to the closed interval [m_i,M_i] for μ-almost every ω; equivalently, m_i ≤ X_i(ω) ≤ M_i almost everywhere.
The real threshold t is strictly positive.
conclusions: The real measure of the event {ω ∈ Ω | Σ_{i∈ι} (X_i(ω) - ∫_Ω X_i(y) dμ(y)) ≥ t} is at most exp(-(c t^2)/(Σ_{i∈ι} ||M_i - m_i||^2)).
There is no multiplicative prefactor in front of exp, and the division denominator is the entire sum Σ_{i∈ι} ||M_i - m_i||^2.
mathematical_definitions: For each i, E_μ[X_i] means the real Bochner integral ∫_Ω X_i(y) dμ(y).
Define the centered finite sum S(ω) = Σ_{i∈ι}(X_i(ω) - E_μ[X_i]).
Define the upper-tail event A_t = {ω ∈ Ω | S(ω) ≥ t}; the inequality uses the inclusive upper tail ≥ t.
Define D = Σ_{i∈ι} ||M_i - m_i||^2 = Σ_{i∈ι}|M_i - m_i|^2. The exponent is exactly -(c t^2)/D, parsed as the negation of the quotient whose denominator is all of D.
The notation μ.real(A_t) denotes ENNReal.toReal(μ(A_t)); because μ is a probability measure, this is the ordinary real probability of A_t.
Real division in Lean is total: if D = 0 then (c t^2)/D = 0, so the right-hand side becomes exp(0) = 1.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a single absolute real constant c > 0 such that, for every finite index set, every probability space, every finite mutually independent family of measurable real random variables X_i, every pair of real bound families m_i and M_i satisfying m_i ≤ X_i ≤ M_i almost everywhere, and every t > 0, the probability that the centered sum Σ_i (X_i - E_μ[X_i]) is at least t is no greater than exp(-(c t^2)/(Σ_i |M_i-m_i|^2)). The displayed bound has no leading prefactor, and the whole sum of squared interval widths is the denominator. Under Lean's total real division, a zero denominator makes the quotient zero and hence the right side one.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The index domain must be finite, although it may be empty; for an empty index type the centered sum and denominator sum are both zero, and t > 0 makes the upper-tail event empty.
Only real-valued random variables and the Borel measurable structure on ℝ are covered.
The result is a one-sided upper-tail estimate with the inclusive event S ≥ t; it does not state a lower-tail or two-sided estimate.
Both c and t are strictly positive. Thresholds t ≤ 0 are not included.
The interval bounds hold only μ-almost everywhere, separately for each index.

No explicit assumptions m_i ≤ M_i are present. If for some i the interval hypothesis is impossible almost everywhere, the implication is vacuous; when its antecedent is satisfiable on a probability space, that hypothesis enforces the needed order almost everywhere.
No explicit integrability hypothesis is present. The Bochner integral is a total Lean definition; in the intended satisfiable bounded measurable probability setting, each X_i is integrable.

The denominator is not assumed positive or nonzero. Lean's total real division sends division by zero to zero here, so a zero denominator yields the trivial right-hand side 1 rather than an undefined expression.
The measure on the left is converted from ENNReal to ℝ by toReal. The probability-measure hypothesis keeps event measures finite.
The existential witness c is uniform over all later binders and therefore cannot depend on the family size, the space, μ, X, m, M, or t.
The conclusion has no multiplicative constant or factor outside the exponential and no additional numeric coefficient has been inserted into its exponent.
